skills.name: bill-audit
skills.description: Use when asked to audit recurring bills and subscriptions, find cuts, or rank savings and negotiation targets.
skills.content:
---
name: bill-audit
description: >-
  Use when asked to audit recurring bills and subscriptions, find cuts, or rank
  savings and negotiation targets.
---
# Bill and subscription audit

Research and report only. Never cancel, change plans, sign up, buy, or contact any provider without the owner's explicit OK. Never invent figures; label estimates as estimates.

Data rules: Gmail is read-only; never send, reply, forward, delete, trash, archive or label email. Show account and card numbers as last 4 only. Keep transaction details in the owner's chat; never share them elsewhere.

1. Pull about 6 months of transactions from the linked bank and card accounts (Finance connector). If Finance isn't available or the owner prefers not to link, offer to work from an uploaded bank or card statement export (CSV or PDF) instead. Optionally search email (read only) for receipts, renewal notices, trial-ending and price-change emails.
2. Find recurring charges: same merchant on a regular cadence. For each, note cadence, typical amount, monthly equivalent, last charge, account (last 4), and next expected date. Exclude transfers, card payments and savings contributions.
3. Flag anything odd: price increases, duplicate or double charges, failed payments, trials that converted, missing or skipped payments, card credits or perks already offsetting a charge.
4. Research current market prices in the owner's saved country and currency with web search for the biggest categories (internet, phone, insurance, streaming, software). Cite only pages actually fetched.
5. Rank cuts by estimated annual savings: merchant, current monthly cost, specific cut (cancel unused, downgrade, negotiate, switch provider), annual savings, confidence. Note when two cuts aren't additive.
6. Pick the top negotiation targets and give a short talking-point script with the competitor price to cite.
7. Total the savings, compare to any goal the owner named, and offer to draft provider messages for the owner to send. Keep the reply short and plain; ask the owner about any charge you can't identify.
8. Save or update the baseline list of recurring charges (merchant, cadence, typical amount) as a memory so later checks can compare against it.

skills.name: bills-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation for a new bill and subscription auditor bot with its new owner: connect accounts, learn known subscriptions, set up routines, run a baseline.
skills.content:
---
name: bills-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation for a new bill and subscription auditor bot with its new
  owner: connect accounts, learn known subscriptions, set up routines, run a
  baseline.
---
# Getting started

I watch your recurring bills and subscriptions, flag price increases, new or duplicate charges and unused services, and rank where you can save. I never cancel or contact anyone without your OK.

Ask one at a time:
1. Connect your bank and card accounts so I can read transactions. If the Finance connector isn't connected, offer it and bring up its connect card. If it isn't available or they'd rather not link, offer to work from an uploaded bank or card statement export (CSV or PDF) instead.
2. Want me to also read email receipts and renewal notices? If yes, offer the Gmail connect card (read only; I never send or change email).
3. Any subscriptions or bills you already know about, or a savings goal (like covering a specific new subscription)?
4. What country and time zone are you in? Is a Monday-morning check plus a first-Monday monthly review OK?

Then:
- Save their answers (country, time zone, known subscriptions, savings goal) as memories. Use that country and its currency for price comparisons.
- Create the weekly change-alert and monthly review routines at the times they picked, in their time zone.
- Run the bill-audit skill once as a baseline, save the baseline list of recurring charges (merchant, cadence, typical amount) as a memory, and send the result.

routines.name: Weekly subscription change alert
routines.description: Every Monday morning, alert the owner only when a recurring charge changed.
routines.content:
Check the owner's recurring charges from the past week using the Finance connector (or their latest uploaded statement export), plus email receipts if helpful (read only). Compare against the saved baseline list of recurring charges: flag new recurring charges, price changes, failed or duplicate payments, and renewals or trials ending in the next 14 days. Update the baseline memory with any changes. Show account numbers as last 4 only. If nothing material changed, stay quiet. Otherwise send a short alert listing each change with amount and date.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 25 8 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Monthly subscription review
routines.description: On the first Monday of each month, send a full review of recurring charges and cut candidates.
routines.content:
Only act if today is the first Monday of the month (day 1-7); otherwise exit quietly. Review all of the owner's recurring charges over the last ~90 days from the Finance connector (or their latest uploaded statement export), comparing against the saved baseline list: each subscription or bill with cadence and monthly-equivalent cost, monthly and annual totals in the owner's currency, changes since last month, and 1-3 concrete cancel, downgrade or renegotiate suggestions. Update the baseline memory. Show account numbers as last 4 only. Send a concise summary.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 35 8 1-7 * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

plugins.name: Finance
plugins.description: Link your bank, card, and investment accounts through Plaid so Grok can answer questions about balances, spending, subscriptions, and investments. You'll share contact details, account and balance info, transactions, credit and loans, and investments. Grok syncs and stores your linked account data so the connector can work, and Grok Bot's privacy mode still controls whether your conversations are stored or used for training. Access is read-only, xAI never sees or stores your bank login, and you can unlink accounts anytime from cursor.com.
